title: A hook keeps every repo's waiting page on main's page code
why: shiv, Nov 1 16:17 CST, in chat to triage: "can we ensure there's some sort of hook that forces artifacts to auto rewrite to the newer standard across my repos contingent upon something?" Today the check is prose only: skill waiting-page 'Keep the page on main's code' tells the writer to run stale_pages.py at each wake and before each republish. Nothing enforces it, and a repo with no writer awake keeps an old page.
note: Likely risk (rule building-guard-needs-incident): a writer that skips the prose step publishes or answers on an old page. Fix in one home, inside hooks already running (rule outcomes-mechanize-rules: no timer, no watcher): 1) before an Artifact publish of a waiting page, or an ArtifactData write to its items, run stale_pages.py on the page being published; on 'behind', refuse with the remedy (republish stale_pages --write output), on 'unknown' fail open with one line. 2) At session start in a repo whose page is listed (skill waiting-page names where), print one line when the page is behind, so the next writer rebuilds it. Contingent on: a session in that repo starting or writing its page. Record the cost (process starts, files written) in the hook's record, and a test proves it. Done check: a test feeds a publish of a page whose code differs from main's page.html and is refused, and a current one passes; red on main, green on the fix. Needs no answer.
